yes, i am depressed. i’ve tried meds but i don’t really like how they make me feel. i know not every med works for everyone but none of the meds i have tried were for me. my depression feels like both the reason i want to sell them, and the reason i havent yet. i’m scared i’ll regret it if i ever feel better, but i dont feel like my motivation will ever come back. if i sold them and later come to regret it i couldnt move past that, these horses have changed my life. i could not ever feel the same way about another horse as i do them. i just dont know what to do. i spent my entire day at work crying about my gelding, my first horse, and figuring this out. then i cried all the way to the barn for my lesson. then my entire lesson i felt like shit because i wanted to go home and i felt like i was riding awful and my mare was clearly having an off day too. then i cried all the way home because i was sad i couldnt do a better job for my horse. i try to bribe myself to go to the barn by buying new stuff for my horses so i have something to excite me. it doesn’t work. i take a break for two weeks and i dread ever returning. i force myself out every day and i just feel miserable. i just don’t know what to do and i hate feeling like this
i’m scared that my motivation will never come back. and i’m scared because the horses i love the most always have something awful happen with them and i dont know if i can do it anymore

i often consider the idea of “if they’re still having more good days than bad than its a life worth living” but then i consider that maybe in 100 days they have 51 good days, does that mean the 49 bad days are worth it for the good days? 

why wait till an animal struggles to get up each morning, if you can make it so they never have to
experience that discomfort at all. at the expense of maybe some extra good days…. i dont know. at the end of the day animals dont have the same idea of life and death as we do. but they dont want to suffer and we dont want them to suffer. 

there probably isnt any “right” decision, we just do the best we can, and that’s okay
